animation.init: Initialize: build a ({{m}}+1) × ({{n}}+1) DP table. Row 0 and column 0 stand for the empty string, so their LCS length is 0
animation.match: Fill dp[{{i}}][{{j}}]: textA[{{i}}-1] and textB[{{j}}-1] are both '{{char}}' — a match! Take the upper-left cell plus 1: dp[{{i}}-1][{{j}}-1] + 1 = {{diag}} + 1 = {{dpVal}}
animation.no_match: Fill dp[{{i}}][{{j}}]: '{{charA}}' ≠ '{{charB}}', no match. Take the larger of the cell above and the cell to the left: max({{up}}, {{left}}) = {{dpVal}}
animation.trace_start: Table filled — the LCS length is dp[{{i}}][{{j}}] = {{length}}. Now backtrack from the bottom-right corner to recover the subsequence itself
animation.trace_match: Both characters at dp[{{i}}][{{j}}] are '{{char}}', so it belongs to the LCS! Move to the upper-left. Subsequence so far: '{{lcs}}'
animation.trace_up: No match, and above ({{up}}) ≥ left ({{left}}): this value was inherited from above, so move up
animation.trace_left: No match, and left ({{left}}) > above ({{up}}): this value was inherited from the left, so move left
animation.done: Backtracking complete! The longest common subsequence is '{{lcs}}' with length {{length}}
animation.done_empty: One of the strings is empty, so the LCS length is 0

ui.runTooltip: Run LCS: fill the DP table, then backtrack the subsequence (up to 8 characters per string)
